comparison: Both support ATG14 expression patterns (C1, C2, C3, C5). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of immunofluorescence and qRT-PCR data, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted these claims by describing findings as 'novel' and 'convincing' without raising concerns. OpenEval also addresses C4 (temporal correlation with implantation window) which was not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Perfect agreement on conditional knockout validation (C6-C11). Both evaluations affirm the genetic model with OpenEval detailing the complementary techniques (qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, histology) and peer reviewers explicitly praising the genetic approach and describing findings as 'likely reproducible.'

Complete agreement on infertility phenotype (C12-C14). Both strongly support the complete infertility finding with OpenEval emphasizing the breeding trial data and complete penetrance, while peer reviewers accepted this as a major finding central to all summaries.

Full agreement on implantation failure (C15-C19). Both evaluations support the claims with OpenEval detailing the multiple lines of evidence (morphology, histology, immunofluorescence) and peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'impaired embryo implantation' and 'faulty uterine receptivity' without critique.

Strong agreement on hormone response mechanisms (C21-C29). OpenEval addresses C20-C29 while peer review covers C21-C29. Both support differential E2 vs E2+P4 responses and the conclusion that phenotype is uterine-specific rather than hormonal. Peer reviewers accepted findings about 'faulty uterine receptivity and decidualization.'

Both support embryo transport defect (C30-C34), though peer review also includes C35-C37 and C134-C137 which OpenEval addresses separately. Both evaluations affirm the embryo retention phenotype as a major finding with peer reviewers explicitly stating 'retention of embryos within the oviduct' and 'impaired embryo transport.'

OpenEval addresses developmental delay and histological confirmation (C35-C37) while peer review groups these with broader embryo retention claims (C30-C37, C134-C137). Both support the findings, though OpenEval notes the 'higher' developmental delay claim is somewhat qualitative and would benefit from statistical analysis.

Perfect agreement on regional ATG14 deletion and autophagy dysfunction (C38-C40). Both evaluations support the mechanistic link between autophagy loss and embryo retention, with peer reviewers accepting this as central to the phenotype explanation.

Complete agreement on oviduct structural abnormalities (C41-C46). Both strongly support the histological findings with OpenEval detailing cellular pathology and regional specificity, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed 'excessive pyroptosis in the oviductal epithelial cells that compromises cellular integrity and structure.'

OpenEval addresses oviduct anatomy background (C47-C51) while peer review focuses on Foxj1-Cre experiment (C50-C58). Both support reduced cell populations in isthmus (C50-C51), with overlap on these specific claims but different scope of evaluation.

Strong agreement on ciliary function being dispensable (C52-C58). Both evaluations accept the Foxj1-Cre negative result as important for mechanism, with peer reviewers praising the 'genetic and pharmacological approaches' and accepting that cilia are not responsible for the phenotype.

OpenEval addresses super-ovulation validation (C134-C137) while peer review groups these with natural mating embryo retention data. Both support the transport defect with OpenEval noting this provides additional validation with higher embryo numbers.

Perfect agreement on mitochondrial dysfunction (C59-C65). Both strongly support these findings with OpenEval emphasizing convergent evidence from multiple techniques (TEM, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR) and peer reviewers accepting ATG14's role 'in preserving mitochondrial structural and functional integrity.'

Strong agreement on pyroptosis activation (C66-C71). OpenEval addresses C66-C71 while peer review focuses on C67-C71. Both strongly support pyroptosis as a novel finding with peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'a novel function of ATG14 in preventing pyroptosis' and accepting tissue-specific activation.

Both address tissue-specific pyroptosis (C122). OpenEval includes this in broader pyroptosis evaluation (C66-C71, including C122 mentioned in text) while peer review separately affirms tissue specificity. Both accept the immunohistochemistry evidence without question.

Complete agreement on pharmacological validation (C72-C78). Both strongly support polyphyllin VI experiments with peer reviewers explicitly praising 'both genetic and pharmacological approaches' and describing findings as 'high-impact and likely reproducible.' OpenEval notes technical challenges and partial penetrance compared to genetic model.

Both address the novel function of ATG14 (C110-C111). OpenEval groups these with extensive background claims (C79-C111) while peer review specifically highlights these as the central novel finding. Both affirm this as exciting, novel, and clinically significant for reproductive medicine.

Minimal overlap on ATG14's unique function among autophagy genes (C125-C126). OpenEval includes these in broader discussion context (C79-C111) while peer review specifically addresses the distinction from other autophagy genes. Both accept the unique nature of ATG14 compared to Fip200, Atg16l, and Becn1.

OpenEval evaluates mouse line and reagent documentation (C112-C115) from methods section. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not comment on materials and methods documentation.

OpenEval evaluates extensive discussion points and literature context (C116-C133). Peer review only addresses small subset (C122, C125-C126) in different contexts. Most discussion claims were not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.
